Stuart Broad has the new ball in his hand and is ready to begin proceedings. Let's play...
... SECOND INNINGS ...

Australia will be really disappointed mostly with their catching because their bowlers created a lot of chances for them. They took time to get suited to the conditions but didn't let the hosts get away with it. They could have restricted England to a lower total than this if they took their five dropped catches which could make a difference. Mitchell Starc was the pick of the bowler again with four wickets while Josh Hazlewood and Todd Murphy got a couple each. Pat Cummins who bowled really well chipped in with the one. Join us in a bit for Australia's reply.

England have been finally bowled out for 283! It was a solid batting performance from them considering the conditions out there. The two openers got them to a very good start adding 62 together. However, Ben Duckett was dismissed for 41 and they suffered a mini collapse as they went from 62-0 to 73-3. However, Harry Brook was brilliant and took his chance well after getting dropped on 5 by Alex Carey. He was the top scorer for them with an excellent 85 while Moeen Ali supported him well before he suffered a groin injury and had to go all-out attack which resulted in his downfall. Even though they lost a couple of wickets in quick succession, crucial contributions from Chris Woakes and Mark Wood took them to a good total.

Australia will hope that their batters are able to play England out of this game with their batting effort.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the third and final session of Day 1 as the umpires make their way out to the middle. The Australian players have taken their respective positions on the field and will be eager to bowl out their opponents in quick time. Chris Woakes and Mark Wood will hope to add as many runs as possible and push their team beyond the 300-run mark. Mitchell Starc has the ball in his hand and will begin proceedings. Let's go...
... DAY 1, SESSION 3 ...

Chris Woakes and Mark Wood have added 38 runs in 45 balls for the eighth wicket as they look to take their team to a reasonable first-inning total. Australia will be thrilled with their bowling effort so far as they have managed to run through the English batting order within two sessions. They will be hoping that the tail does not wag for the hosts and they can wrap this inning up at the earliest. Moeen Ali was dismissed by Todd Murphy in his very first over and that opened the floodgates as wickets fell in a bundle. Mitchell Starc managed to dismiss the English skipper and Josh Hazlewood claimed his second of the game with the dismissal of Jonny Bairstow. Starc then got the big wicket of Harry Brook but the Australian pacers have been taken for a few runs by the two English fast bowlers. Do join us at 8.30 pm IST (3 pm GMT) to find out how the last session of Day 1 in this final Ashes Test plays out.

SESSION SUMMARY - 119 runs and 4 wickets in 24 overs. Another session that began really well for the hosts but a bunch of wickets towards the end has shifted the momentum firmly in favour of the visitors. The game has moved on at a fast pace and England have continued with their attacking intent despite the fall of wickets. They went into Lunch having lost three wickets and with 131 runs on the board. Harry Brook was two runs short of his fifty and reached his landmark soon after the break. He added 111 runs for the fourth wicket in just 108 balls with Moeen Ali who seemed to injure his groin during his inning. He changed his strategy after receiving treatment and began to go after the bowlers but lost his wicket in the quest to be aggressive. Ben Stokes and Jonny Bairstow could not trouble the batters much and when Harry Brook was dismissed on 85 in 91 deliveries, England looked to be in all sorts of trouble.

It could have been worse for England, but the visitors were really poor with their catching as they dropped a few too many as per their standards. Harry Brook took full advantage of this and racked up the runs and is already into the 40s while Moeen Ali also held the other end well. Both these batters will look to build this stand even further in the post-Lunch session while Australia will hope to make some early inroads and expose the lower middle order of the hosts as soon as possible. Join us at 6.10 pm IST (12.40 pm GMT) to see how things pan out in the second session.

After being forced to bat first, the two English openers, Ben Duckett and Zak Crawley got off to a flying start adding 62 runs in no time. The Aussie pacers couldn't use the overcast conditions that well but once the skipper Pat Cummins came into the attack, things started to happen and he was good with the changes as well. Just at the hour mark, Mitchell Marsh got rid of Duckett with one straying down the leg which was followed by two quick wickets from Josh Hazlewood and Mitchell Starc to reduce the hosts from 62-0 to 73-3.

SESSION SUMMARY - 131 runs and 3 wickets in 26 overs. A session of two halves! England scored runs at a pretty good rate and there were a lot of boundaries, but Australia too managed to get the breakthroughs and haven't let the hosts get away with it. It was full of exciting cricket as both teams went hard at each other and we can expect the same throughout this final Test.

Commentary.Commentary: We are done with the prematch formalities as the umpires walk out to the middle. The Australian players are taking their respective positions on the field as Zak Crawley and Ben Duckett stride to the centre to open the inning for England. They will want to get a good partnership going here under overcast conditions in order to protect their middle order. Mitchell Starc has the new ball in his hand and is ready to begin proceedings. Let's play...

We are moments away from the start of the game as the two sets of players and the match officials line up for the national anthems. It will be the national anthem of Australia first followed by England's national anthem.

Ben Stokes, the captain of England says that they would have had a bowl first as well. Explains that the conditions are overcast and also they have done better bowling first. Claims that they know what team they are going to go with, a couple of days in advance so there is no point in waiting. Adds that it gives the lads who are selected get time to prepare. Reckons that both teams come into this game to win. Ends by saying that the Aussies have already retained the Ashes but will want to win the series and they themselves want to level it.

Pat Cummins, the skipper of Australia says that they will bowl first as there is a bit of cloud cover overhead. Adds that the wicket looks good and they still wish that they would have gone one better when they played here four years ago. Mentions that the preparation has been good and they are excited about this. Informs Todd Murphy is in for Cameron Green. Says Lyon always bowled well here and Murphy can be useful too.

Australia (Playing XI) - David Warner, Usman Khawaja, Marnus Labuschagne, Steven Smith, Travis Head, Mitchell Marsh, Alex Carey (WK), Mitchell Starc, Pat Cummins (C), Todd Murphy (In place of Cameron Green), Josh Hazlewood

TOSS - Pat Cummins calls it right and the coin lands in his favour. Australia have elected to BOWL first.

England will need to pick themselves from the disappointment they faced in the last Test match and Ben Stokes will be absolutely thrilled with a drawn series after losing the first two games. They have already announced an unchanged side for this game and have found some good momentum. They have had to tweak their batting order due to the injury to Ollie Pope, but the leadership crew's backing has helped the batters to play positively. Their weakness is their spin bowling department as they depend on two part-time spinners in the form of Moeen Ali and Joe Root. Their seasoned fast-bowling campaigners James Anderson and Stuart Broad may be playing their last Ashes and have worked hard through the series but the tide turned in favour of the hosts with the introduction of Chris Woakes and Mark Wood to the side. Stay tuned as we bring you the toss and team updates.

Australia have managed to retain the Ashes with a game to spare courtesy of the rain gods but will be hunting for their third win to make this a comprehensive series victory. They are back at the venue where they recently won the World Test Championship and it will be apt for them to win their final Test of the tour in the manner in which they started it. Australia are expected to make one change as they will look to get Todd Murphy back into the playing eleven. Nathan Lyon has been a massive miss for the visitors and they do not seem to be coping with his loss too well. The Aussie batters have contributed at some point through the series but have lacked the consistency that makes them ever so lethal. The pace bowlers have been among the wickets but have found it difficult to contain the English batters and the Aussies will be hoping to find their mojo back in this tie.

Hello, and a warm welcome, ladies and gentlemen to our coverage of the fifth and final Test match in the Ashes where barring the two rain-filled days in Manchester in the last Test match, we have witnessed some of the most intriguing action in red-ball cricket. Australia had taken an early 2-0 lead in the series by winning the first two matches in Edgbaston and at the Lord’s but England came back strong in Headingley. The hosts dominated most of the game at Old Trafford before rain played spoilsport, ruining a golden opportunity for them to level the series. The focus is now on the series finale at the Kennington Oval in London where Australia can win their first series in England since 2001 or it is to be seen if England can level the series.
